land.text: 'The Japanese returned China Weihaiwei on 24 May 1898, after which it was occupied by the British'

predecessors.note: The Japanese had occupied it from 1895 in the Battle of Weihaiwei (page); that occupation ended before this state's start.

land.text: 'returned to the Republic of China on 1 October 1930'; Liugong Island and its facilities 'leased back to the U.K. until 1940'

capitals.name: Port Edward
capitals.note: The page: Port Edward 'served as the capital', 'the center of the original Weihai city, now in Huancui District'. Coordinates are the modern city centre.

correction.text: the British leasehold at Weihai with Liugong Island, on the northern coast of the Shandong Peninsula

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no Weihaiwei row. The page gives no area for the leasehold (only modern development-zone areas) and is silent on the coastal belt; it names Liugong Island, which 'protects the port', with a Royal Navy base. A radius of 18 km round Weihai (2 cells, 506 km2 on the grid) is a pure stand-in. No infobox area.

region.text: Weihaiwei and Liugong Island, leased to Britain

ledger.note: 1 July 1898: the core area 'was ruled by the British from 1 July 1898 to 1930 under a lease agreement with the Chinese empire'; 'The Japanese returned China Weihaiwei on 24 May 1898, after which it was occupied by the British.' The page is silent on the Convention of Peking and on the lease's length.
1 October 1930: 'became an integral part of China after it was returned to the Republic of China on 1 October 1930'. Liugong Island and its facilities were 'leased back to the U.K. until 1940'.

certainty.note: The page gives neither an area nor a boundary for the leasehold; the radius is a stand-in.

sources.title: Weihaiwei
sources.note: Japanese occupation 1895; return to China 24 May 1898; British rule from 1 July 1898; return on 1 October 1930; Liugong Island leased back to 1940; Port Edward the capital; no area for the leasehold.

notes: Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-25 from one page (the Foreign concessions in China page was silent and is not cited). Not settled: (1) the leasehold's area and the coastal belt are not on the page; the radius is a guess. (2) The British side: the page does not name the British department that ran it; the counterpart for the metropole is the British colonial empire (Cliopatria: British Colonial Empire, 1706-1999), which carries no matching event. (3) The page gives the Japanese occupation as 1895-1898 only in a sentence about the battle. (4) Liugong Island stayed British to 1940, after the dossier ends. Counterpart qing-dynasty (ea-08-a/b).
